nodes.text: Facing an ATO Audit? Get expert help

nodes.html: An ATO audit or review is stressful — but you do not have to face it alone. A registered tax agent can manage the ATO's correspondence, prepare the requested information, negotiate outcomes, and lodge objections on your behalf. Your Accountant Match connects you with a local agent experienced in ATO audits, disputes and debt matters.

nodes.html: ATO contact ranges from a simple data-matching query (a letter asking about a discrepancy) through to a full audit of deductions, income, GST or payroll. Most start as a review and escalate only if issues are found. Engaging a registered agent early — at the first letter, not the final demand — keeps the matter contained and reduces the risk of escalation.

nodes.html: What a registered agent does during an audit
nodes.text: What a registered agent does during an audit

nodes.html: A registered tax agent receives ATO correspondence on your behalf, prepares and reviews the information requested, manages the timeline, explains your position to the ATO, and negotiates outcomes. If the ATO issues an amended assessment you disagree with, the agent can lodge an objection and, if needed, escalate to the Administrative Review Tribunal (ART) — which replaced the former Administrative Appeals Tribunal (AAT) on 14 October 2024. You stay in control of decisions; the agent handles the process.

nodes.html: If an audit results in a tax debt, a registered agent can negotiate a payment plan that spreads the liability over time, request remission of penalties and interest where grounds exist, and stop enforcement actions like garnishee orders or director penalty notices. The goal is a sustainable arrangement that lets you move forward.

nodes.q: What should I do if I get an ATO audit letter?
nodes.a: Do not ignore it. Engage a registered tax agent immediately — at the first letter, not the final demand. The agent manages ATO correspondence, prepares the requested information, and negotiates outcomes. Early engagement keeps the matter contained and reduces escalation risk.
nodes.aText: Do not ignore it. Engage a registered tax agent immediately — at the first letter, not the final demand. The agent manages ATO correspondence, prepares the requested information, and negotiates outcomes. Early engagement keeps the matter contained and reduces escalation risk.

nodes.q: Can a tax agent represent me to the ATO?
nodes.a: Yes — that is a core right of TPB registration. A registered agent can receive your ATO correspondence, respond to queries, negotiate payment plans, lodge objections, and represent you in disputes. Tell us you need audit or dispute support in the questionnaire.
nodes.aText: Yes — that is a core right of TPB registration. A registered agent can receive your ATO correspondence, respond to queries, negotiate payment plans, lodge objections, and represent you in disputes. Tell us you need audit or dispute support in the questionnaire.

nodes.q: How much does ATO audit help cost?
nodes.a: It depends on complexity. A simple data-matching query may be a few hundred dollars; a full audit with objections can be several thousand. The matched agent quotes after assessing the scope. The matching service itself is free.
nodes.aText: It depends on complexity. A simple data-matching query may be a few hundred dollars; a full audit with objections can be several thousand. The matched agent quotes after assessing the scope. The matching service itself is free.

nodes.q: Can I dispute an ATO amended assessment?
nodes.a: Yes. A registered agent can lodge an objection to an amended assessment, and if the objection is disallowed, escalate to the Administrative Review Tribunal (ART) — which replaced the former Administrative Appeals Tribunal (AAT) on 14 October 2024. There are strict time limits (typically 60 days for objections), so act quickly.
nodes.aText: Yes. A registered agent can lodge an objection to an amended assessment, and if the objection is disallowed, escalate to the Administrative Review Tribunal (ART) — which replaced the former Administrative Appeals Tribunal (AAT) on 14 October 2024. There are strict time limits (typically 60 days for objections), so act quickly.

nodes.q: What's the difference between an ATO review and a full audit?
nodes.a: An ATO review is a narrower check of specific items (often data-matching), while a full audit examines a broader area in depth. Most matters start as a review and escalate only if issues are found. Engaging an agent at the review stage often prevents escalation to a full audit.
nodes.aText: An ATO review is a narrower check of specific items (often data-matching), while a full audit examines a broader area in depth. Most matters start as a review and escalate only if issues are found. Engaging an agent at the review stage often prevents escalation to a full audit.

nodes.q: Can an agent negotiate an ATO payment plan for audit debt?
nodes.a: Yes. If an audit results in tax debt, a registered agent can negotiate a payment plan, request remission of penalties and interest where grounds exist, and stop enforcement actions like garnishee orders or director penalty notices.
nodes.aText: Yes. If an audit results in tax debt, a registered agent can negotiate a payment plan, request remission of penalties and interest where grounds exist, and stop enforcement actions like garnishee orders or director penalty notices.

nodes.q: How quickly can I get an ATO-audit-experienced agent?
nodes.a: Most matches are completed within 60 seconds of finishing the questionnaire. Your matched firm will typically reach out within 2 hours, or you can call for immediate assistance if your ATO matter is time-sensitive.
nodes.aText: Most matches are completed within 60 seconds of finishing the questionnaire. Your matched firm will typically reach out within 2 hours, or you can call for immediate assistance if your ATO matter is time-sensitive.

nodes.q: Will engaging an agent make the ATO suspicious?
nodes.a: No. Using a registered tax agent is entirely normal and expected — it signals you are taking the matter seriously. The ATO deals with agents every day and generally prefers correspondence through a registered representative.
nodes.aText: No. Using a registered tax agent is entirely normal and expected — it signals you are taking the matter seriously. The ATO deals with agents every day and generally prefers correspondence through a registered representative.
